_doc: How people greet you and part from you. Speaker = the NPC; {first} is YOU, {addr} how they address you, {named} the same with a name. Tags: spouse child parent sibling kin stranger friend hostile sweetheart betrothed debtor grudge favoured holy market night hungry tired unhappy cheerful beggar.

start.t: There you are, {first}. I was only just thinking of you.
Come in, my love, and sit a while. The work will keep.
{First}! Come here. Let me look at you.
A good {part} to you, {addr}. Was it a hard day?
Ah, {first}. Something you want?
Oh. It's you.
We have said all there is to say, {first}, and then some.
{First}! My own dear {kin}. Come, tell me everything.
Well, {first}. What mischief now?
Come here, child, you've mud on your face. Now, what is it?
Ha! The prodigal. Come, sit by me.
{First}. You've been told about the work that's waiting.
Speak, {first}. I am listening, though I hardly like your tone of late.
{Addr}! Have you a moment?
{Addr}, I've been waiting for you.
Oh, {addr}... am I in trouble?
Good {part}, {addr}. You're well, I hope?
{Addr}. I'd not thought to see you today.
Ah, {first}. Come to bother me, have you?
{First}! Thank God, someone with sense to talk to.
What do you want, {first}? And don't say you've been looking for me.
Oh, it's you. Our mother would have been ashamed of how we part, you know.
{Addr}! Out and about on a {weather} day, are you?
{Addr}! It is good to see my own blood on an ordinary day.
Kinsman! Come, sit. How go things with you?
Kinswoman! Come, sit. How go things with you?
Good {part}, {addr}. Family should talk more than it does.
Ah. {First}. Well, we are family, whatever else.
Oh! {First}. I... was hoping you might pass this way.
There you are. I had begun to think you'd forgotten me.
Well met, {first}. You've a way of arriving just when I'm idle.
{First}. My heart is not so hard as I pretended.
My betrothed! The whole village talks of nothing else.
Good {part}, {first}. You seek me out again, I see.
{First}! A friendly face. Sit, sit.
Ha, {first}! I'd know that step anywhere. What news?
Well met, friend. The day is better for it.
Good {part}, {first}. I've a spare moment for you, as always.
{First}, my friend! Come, let's talk of something other than work.
God keep you, {addr}. How may I serve?
{Addr}. Your pardon — you wish a word with me?
My {addr}, an honour. What would you have of me?
At your service, {addr}.
Peace to you, {addr}. I hope I give no offence.
Good {part}, {addr}. I'm not used to such visitors.
Good {part}, friend. Do I know you?
Well met, stranger. You're not from here, I think.
Good {part}. Have you business in {place}?
Who's this, then? Speak up, I'm listening.
Hello! Are you new here? I don't know your face.
Well? What do you want?
Speak, then. I haven't all day to stand about.
You. Yes, you. What is it?
Ah. Yes? You may speak.
Hm. Good {part}, I suppose. Who are you?
Good {part}, {first}.
Ah, {first}. How goes the day?
Well met, {first}. Something on your mind?
{First}. Good to see you about.
Morning, {first}.
Afternoon, {first}. Lovely, isn't it?
Evening, {first}. Getting on for supper.
A blessed holy day to you, {first}.
Busy market, {first}. Mind your purse.
Hm. {First}. What is it?
Yes? Be quick about it, {first}.
I'd rather you had passed by, {first}. But since you're here...
What now? Make it brief.
God and Mary to you, {first}.
God save all here. Good {part}, {first}.
Dieu vous garde, {first}.
Bore da, {first}. A fair morning, if the Lord allows.
Heill, {first}. Hale and happy to you.
Gott grüß dich, {first}. Good {part}.
Peace be with you, {first}.
God's blessing on this holy day, my {addr}.
Brother in Christ. Come in, the church is quiet.
Alms for the poor, {addr}, for the love of God?
A penny for a hungry soul, {addr}?
Pardon, {addr}. My belly is loud and my temper short. What is it?
I'm half asleep on my feet, {first}. Speak, I'll try to follow.
I'm in a rare good humour, {first}! What can I do for you?
Don't mind my face, {first}, it's been a poor day.
Out in the {weather}, {addr}? Come in out of it if you like.
Hello! Hello, {addr}! Are you going to talk to me?
Good {part}, {addr}. I was just remarking the {weather}.
Sister in Christ. Come in, the church is quiet.

refuse: {Self} turns away. "I have nothing to say to you."
"I'll not speak with you, not after what you did."
"Go on your way. We're done, you and I."

refuse.t: "You'd best leave before my temper rises."

debt: By the way, {first} — you still owe me {money}.
I'll not ask twice, but you know you owe me {money}.
A word, {first}: {money}, when you can. I've mouths to feed.

debt.t: Don't forget the {money}, {addr}. I do not forget.
Take your time with that {money}, {first}. But not too much of it.

grudge: Mind your tongue, {first}. I remember how you {memory}.

grudge.t: A man — or woman — remembers when you {memory}.
I'll hear you, but I recall well enough that you {memory}.

grudge: It's not so easy, {first}, after you {memory}.
favoured: I've not forgotten how you {memory}, {first}. I'm grateful.
Remember when you {memory}? I do, and kindly.
You {memory}, and that's not forgotten here.
I think well of you, {first}, since you {memory}.
ambition: I'll tell you something, {first}: all I truly want is {ambition}.
Some day, God willing, I'll have {ambition}.
What I'd like most in all the world is {ambition}.

ambition.t: I work and I wait, {first}. All for {ambition}.
People think I want nothing. But I think often of {ambition}.

ask: Well, I must be going. God keep you.
I'd best be on my way.

ask.t: God and Mary go with you.

reply.t: And you. Mind how you go.
Go safe, {first}. The roads are what they are.
Take your leave, then. I've my work.
Take care of yourself, my love.

cutoff.t: That's enough. I'm done with this conversation.
No more of this! Be gone.
I'll hear no more. Away with you.
You try me too far. Leave.
Good day to you, {addr}. And that's all I'll say.
I will not be spoken to so.

tired.t: We've talked a good deal today, {addr}. I've work waiting.
Surely you've other business than chattering with me?
My ears are tired, {first}. Another day.
We've said what there is to say for now, haven't we?
I can't stand about all day. Come back tomorrow.
Let an old tongue rest, {first}. Come back soon.
Mother of God, {first}, give me a moment's quiet!

repeat.t: You've asked me that already, haven't you?
I've told you what I know.
Nothing's changed since a moment ago, {first}.
